# C&P Exam Prep — Mental Health

> **Status:** active · **Created:** 2026-07-05 · **Updated:** 2026-10-08, second pass. This pass reflects:
> - the veteran's own answers;
> - the supporting documents added to `supporting-docs/` (gitignored), including OCR of the scanned Harmony psychiatric notes;
> - the 07-17-2026 nexus letter as submitted;
> - the two VA Forms 21-4138 signed 10/7/2026.
>
> **Supersedes:**
> - the 2026-07-05 version of this file, whose delusion, daily-care, pre-service and job-history sections were wrong or incomplete;
> - `ClaudeDisabilityAssets/CP-Exam-Prep-Mental-Health-Marcus-Klein.pdf`.
>
> **Detailed companion:** `personal-records/CP-EXAM-STRATEGY-2026-10-13.docx` (private). It has the timeline tables and a 16-item gap-by-gap guide, each item comparing the record with the truth. **Read that first.** This file is the short version.
> **Basis:** `planning-docs/REASSESSMENT-2026-10-08-CP-EXAM.md` (odds, citations), `CLAIM-ASSESSMENT.md`.
> **Purpose:** be ready to give a complete, accurate, consistent account at the C&P exam. The examiner's DBQ is the most influential single item, though legally the rater weighs the whole record (38 CFR 4.126(a)).

## The scheduled exam

- **When:** Tuesday **2026-10-13, 12:00 PM Central**
- **Format:** VES TeleC&P video call. The doxy.me link is in the VES email of 2026-10-07. **VES#:** 227264947760
- **Examiner:** Kasi Howard, PsyD. Psychologist, Texas-licensed, trained for PTSD, MST and mental-disorders exams.
- **Location:** you'll be in Texas.
- **VSO:** James York
- **Bring:** photo ID, and a written list of current medications (name, dose, prescriber).
- **VES:** 877-637-8387, for questions, rescheduling, or if the video fails. For a supplemental claim, failing to report without good cause means the claim "shall be denied" (38 CFR 3.655(b)).

### Before Tuesday

- [ ] Confirm the appointment with VES. Don't rely on the email alone.
- [ ] Run the audio/video pre-check from the VES email, on WiFi, on the device you'll use.
- [ ] Re-read **your own signed statements** once: the personal statement and 21-0781 (both 6/17/2026), and the two 21-4138s (10/7/2026). The goal is to know what you told VA. Don't rehearse.
- [ ] Ask James York:
  - whether VA has **received both 21-4138s**. They correct the perpetrator's status, give your account of pre-service history, and list your full treatment history; they only help if they're in the file.
  - which **nexus letter(s)** VA holds: 7/2, 07-17, or both.
  - whether these are in the file:
    - the **Metal manager statement** (8/2/2026)
    - the **Meta, Metal and MNTN separation documents** (the MNTN copy redacted for severance money)
    - Erica's signed statement
    - Cherie's CPT notes

  Anything still missing goes by fax to Evidence Intake, **844-531-7818**, before the exam.
- [ ] If you see Cherie before Tuesday: make sure she has heard the persecutory worry described as it actually is (see below).
- [ ] Plan to be **sober** for the exam. Intoxication or withdrawal during a psychological exam can make it unusable.

### Exam-day setup

- Take the call **alone, in a private room**, door closed. Erica out of the room and out of earshot. If Dr. Howard wants to hear from Erica, she'll ask, and Erica answers in her own words.
- Join by 11:50, with ID and the medication list within reach.
- Afterward, ask James to request a copy of the completed DBQ.

## The one thing that matters most

**Accuracy beats impact.** Describe your **worst and typical** days, not your best days. Composure on camera isn't evidence of how you function. Be concrete: how often, how bad, real examples, and include things that don't help the claim.

Dr. Howard has the claims file. Answers that match the record build credibility. An answer that doesn't match costs more than any single symptom is worth. In an MST claim, credibility is what service connection turns on.

## The framing

VA rates occupational and social impairment together. Describe both:

- **Work:** concentration, reliability, attendance, leave and accommodations, and what happened at each job (see the job history below).
- **Social:**
  - your marriage as it actually functions now;
  - your real current contact with family and friends;
  - isolation, and what initiating contact costs you.

**What the honest picture supports.** Your own account fits VA's 70% language more naturally than the 100% language. That means "deficiencies in most areas," including "neglect of personal appearance and hygiene" and suicidal ideation.

There is no 90% level for mental disorders (see `REASSESSMENT-2026-10-08-CP-EXAM.md` §1). Don't stretch anything to reach 100%. Make sure the real 70%-level picture comes through clearly and credibly.

## Daily care and self-care

**What's true (your account, 10/8).** Erica schedules your appointments. She also tells you when to:
- cut your hair, shave, shower;
- eat and drink water;
- see doctors and dentists;
- get things fixed, do laundry, clean parts of the house;
- handle general self-care.

That is **prompting and managing**. It is not doing these things for you.

**What the file says:**
- **Erica's signed statement:** she has to "constantly remind him to brush his teeth and shower," she dusts crumbs and dandruff from your face, makes and tracks your appointments, and grocery shops "in an effort to get him to eat proper nutrition." This **matches** your account.
- **Cherie's 07-17 letter:** "During especially bad stretches... his wife takes over for him. She washes and picks out the clothes for him to wear, needs to remind him to brush his teeth..."
- **Cherie's session notes** (May–July 2026): "avoiding self-care practices"; impairment in "Self Care."
- **Harmony psychiatric notes** (Dr. Naficy, five inpatient visits 4/18–5/5/2026): "well-groomed and clean" every time. Cherie's letter attributes inpatient grooming to staff prompting.
- **Internal planning docs only** (`RATING-REPORT-REMEDIATION-PLAN-2026-07-16.md` [CORRECTION 3]) said Erica "feeds him, cuts his hair." That **isn't** what you or Erica describe. Don't adopt it.

**At the exam:**
- Describe exactly what Erica prompts, how often, how long it's been this way, and what gets skipped when she doesn't prompt.
- If you remember what self-care looked like during the Feb–May 2026 separation, that's a concrete real example.
- If the hygiene or "typical day" question doesn't come up, raise it yourself before the end.

## Symptom checklist — describe honestly, don't hide, don't overstate

**Suicidal ideation.** Describe it as a **pattern over time**: when it's present, how often, how intense (passive or more intense), how long bad stretches last, and what quieter stretches are like.

What the record shows:
- **Personal statement (6/17/2026):** "hits every day when I wake up."
- **Denials during the Harmony stay:**
  - FMLA evaluation, 5/14/2026: "denies current SI... history of passive SI"
  - Dr. Naficy's notes at Harmony, 4/18, 4/21, 4/28 and 5/1: "no suicidal thoughts"
  - Dr. Naficy, 5/5: "denies any thoughts of self harm or SI"
  - Harmony discharge, 5/11: "denied suicidal ideation"
- **Cherie's notes:** don't record SI either way.

You weren't having suicidal thoughts in mid-May, which fits the 5/5–5/14 entries. The letter's explanation (denying SI at inpatient admissions to avoid an involuntary hold) applies only where it's actually true. You decide whether it fits any of the April Harmony entries.

_(Corrected 2026-10-08: a 6/25/26 "denies SI" note cited in earlier planning docs does not exist. Cherie's 6/25 note has no SI entry.)_

**The other symptoms:**
- **Depression:** frequency, duration, what an episode looks like day to day, anhedonia, and sleep, appetite and energy.
- **Anxiety and panic:** real frequency. The letter says "more mornings than not and sometimes during the day." Describe the physical symptoms, triggers and duration.
- **OCD:** intrusive thoughts, rituals or checking, how much time they take, and how they interfere. VA lists "obsessional rituals which interfere with routine activities."
- **Hypervigilance and avoidance:** startle, scanning, avoiding reminders, people and settings.
- **Intrusion:** nightmares, intrusive memories.
- **Sleep:** the current pattern and medications.
- **Irritability and anger:** frequency and triggers. Per *Mauerhan* the listed symptoms are examples, so real irritability counts without violence.
- **Concentration and memory:** what you rely on Erica to remember, concretely. Don't round up to the 100%-level "memory loss for names of close relatives, own occupation, or own name" unless that's literally true.
- **Catastrophic beliefs about the world:** describe them as anxious, catastrophic preoccupation you can recognize as probably excessive when you step back. That is how you've described it; don't call it "delusional."
- **Current substance use:** you're struggling with it now. If asked, be honest about what, how much, how often, last use and any treatment. Describe its link to your other symptoms only as you actually experience it.

## The persecutory worry (replaces the old "two delusions" section)

The 2026-07-05 version of this file called two beliefs "confirmed genuine delusions." Your own descriptions on 10/8 don't support that:

- **Persecutory:**
  - It started **after** you left the military, and you describe it as **a recurring worry**.
  - At the exam, if it comes up, describe it as it is: what it's about, how often it comes, how convinced you are while it's happening, whether you can step back from it, and what you do because of it.
  - Don't use the word "delusion"; that's a clinical judgment for the examiner.
  - Dr. Naficy's notes (Apr–May 2026) record "denies... delusions" and "no hallucinations." That fits a worry, not a fixed belief.
- **"Grandiose":** "I believe I'm capable of great things." That's ordinary self-belief, **not a symptom**. Don't present it as one. If asked about grandiosity, answer truthfully.
- **Cherie's letter:** it uses "paranoid delusions" only for the fear of losing your job, and you did lose jobs. Describe the fear, and acknowledge that the losses happened.

## Be ready for these specific questions

**"When did you first tell anyone about the assault?"** This is the most likely hard question. The letter says June 17, 2026, but the MST-based claim was received 5/19/2026. Your true sequence:

| When | Who |
|---|---|
| ~2012–2013, in service | Reyes and Poquette (and Goff, per your personal statement) |
| 2021 | Erica |
| Jan 2022 | Melissa Robbins, Starlite Liberty program. A checklist recorded an "unwanted sexual experience"; EMDR. |
| 2024 | VA claim, **not** MST-based. You had poor guidance. It was denied because VA couldn't get Dr. Charles Bowers's records. |
| 6/17/2026 | Cherie, in full |

Explain in your own words why you told some people and not others, including why you hadn't told Cherie in three years.

**"Why do earlier records deny trauma?"** You may be asked about:
- 2015 VA intake (Jennings CBOC): "denies experiencing military sexual trauma"; negative PTSD screen.
- 2018 Victory, two intakes: "denies at this time."
- 2023–2025 Starlite: "None reported" or "DENIES."

Your own account is genuine denial and active avoidance at the time, not that it didn't happen. Delayed, uneven disclosure is common in male MST survivors. Not reporting an assault isn't evidence it didn't happen (*AZ v. Shinseki*, 731 F.3d 1303).

**The incident.** It was harassment through 2012, ending in an assault. You were incapacitated: you'd been drinking, passed out (not normal for you), and suspect your drink was drugged. Describe the drugging as a suspicion. Memory gaps from incapacitation are expected; say what you remember and what you don't.

The perpetrator was **a co-worker's civilian wife**. Your signed 21-0781 says "service member"; your 21-4138 item 3 corrects that. If asked, give the accurate answer and say you filed a correction. The letter's "single incident trauma" understates the harassment period, so describe both.

**"Your records show substance use and treatment before you enlisted."** This is now one of the most checkable discrepancies in the file.
- **Records:** Victory 2018 (p. 8) lists opioid pills from age 18 and cocaine at 19. Earlier review found Jan 2023 Starlite records also list opioid use and anxiety/depression treatment around 18.
- **Your signed account:**
  - Personal statement: "minor alcohol and maybe a little marijuana."
  - 21-4138 (10/7): no opioids, cocaine or illicit drugs besides marijuana before service, to the best of your recollection; the Victory history was taken the day of a detox admission while actively using; about 2–3 months with a Lake Charles psychiatrist around age 19 for mild anxiety/depression.
- **At the exam:**
  - Acknowledge the pre-service psychiatric treatment plainly.
  - On pre-service drug use, give your honest recollection and the context you actually remember. "To the best of my recollection" is what you signed, and it's an honest standard.
  - Your 21-4138 explains the Victory entry but not the Starlite one. Know your honest answer if Starlite comes up.
  - Describe concretely what changed after 2012.
  - Calm and consistent matters more than perfect.

**"Tell me about your work history."** From the employer documents and your 21-4138:

| Employer | Dates | Leave | How it ended |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meta | 3/28/2022 – 7/28/2023 | FMLA (your account) | Company layoff, WARN notice |
| DISQO | Jul 2023 – Mar 2024 | FMLA (your account) | You know (not in the documents) |
| Metal | 4/15 – 12/6/2024 | No FMLA. Sick leave, schedule flexibility and reassigned work; your manager's statement quotes you calling your condition "debilitating" (7/18/2024). | Headcount reduction for financial reasons |
| Mountain (MNTN) | May 2025 – Jun 2026 | FMLA from 4/17/2026 | Involuntary termination with severance. The agreement's separation date is 6/26/2026; your 21-4138 says 6/30. Use the date you can stand behind. |

- **Say plainly that Meta and Metal were layoffs.** Then describe what work was like anyway: attendance, concentration, leave, accommodations. Presenting layoffs as disability-driven losses would discount the rest; the documented attendance problems are strong on their own.
- **Since June 2026** you haven't been working, and you've left software engineering.
- **The MNTN agreement:** its confidentiality (§9) covers only the severance money, and §18 protects communicating with a government agency. Describing why you separated is fine.

**Things in the 07-17 nexus letter the examiner may ask about.** Confirm only what's accurate:
- **Separation:** you and Erica separated "for a couple of months" (Feb–May 2026, your account); she considered divorce.
- **FMLA "at every job":** true for three of four. Metal was sick leave and accommodations, not FMLA.
- **Social contact:** the letter says that outside Erica and Cherie you regularly speak to no one, that you've been estranged from family for 6–7 years, and that you go on about one social outing a week. You now have **a reasonable amount of contact with family and your brother**. Describe your real current contact honestly: who, how often, who initiates, what it costs.

**The marriage.** The examiner will have three accounts:
- your personal statement: "a healthy and supportive relationship";
- Cherie: "an area of total impairment... caregiving dependency";
- Erica: separation, considered divorce, "didn't want to be his care taker."

Describe it as it is now. If both support and strain are true, say both. Don't try to match any one document.

**"There's an amphetamine-type SUD diagnosis (F15.20) in the Harmony records."** If you don't know what drove that coding, say so rather than inventing an explanation.

**"What does a typical day look like right now?"** This is the chance to give the real current picture, including Erica's prompting, isolation, and substance use. Don't minimize and don't overstate.

## If an inconsistency is raised

If a correction exists for that item, refer to it. Otherwise, say honestly what you remember and what you don't. A real memory gap about a single distant event is normal and credible. Don't manufacture a more specific explanation than you actually have.

## What not to do

- Don't claim symptoms you don't have, or adopt a document's version of events when it isn't accurate. That includes "feeds me," "cuts my hair," "delusions," "every day for years," "estranged from family," and "FMLA at every job."
- Don't minimize out of pride or habit. If you're holding it together on camera, it's fair to say that isn't your average day.
- Don't cite regulations or argue rating levels. Describe your experience.
- Don't let Erica or anyone else prompt you during the call.

## Support

If things get heavy before Tuesday, or substance use escalates:
- **Veterans Crisis Line:** call 988, then press 1; or text 838255. Free, confidential, 24/7.
- **Cherie:** 512-712-0331.
- **SAMHSA National Helpline** (substance use): 1-800-662-4357.
